title: Haggai Chapter 1 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on Haggai chapter 1 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: Haggai Chapter 1 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of Haggai Chapter 1.

questions.question: In which year of King Darius' reign did the word of the LORD come by Haggai the prophet?
questions.explanation: The word of the LORD came in the second year of Darius the king as stated in Haggai 1:1.

questions.question: To whom did the word of the LORD come through Haggai the prophet?
questions.explanation: The word came to Zerubbabel the son of Shealtiel, governor of Judah, and Joshua the son of Josedech, the high priest, as mentioned in Haggai 1:1.

questions.question: What excuse did the people give for not building the LORD's house?
options: We are too few in number
questions.explanation: The people said, 'The time is not come, the time that the LORD'S house should be built' as recorded in Haggai 1:2.

questions.question: Who brought the word of the LORD to the people according to Haggai 1:3?
questions.explanation: The word of the LORD came by Haggai the prophet as stated in Haggai 1:3.

questions.question: What question does the LORD ask the people about their dwellings in Haggai 1?
options: Is it time to dwell in your cieled houses while this house lies waste?
Why do you build your houses so quickly?
Who gave you permission to build your houses?
questions.correctAnswer: Is it time to dwell in your cieled houses while this house lies waste?
questions.explanation: The LORD asks if it is time for them to dwell in their cieled houses while the temple lies waste as recorded in Haggai 1:4.

questions.question: What does the LORD command the people to do in Haggai 1:5?
questions.explanation: The LORD commands them to 'Consider your ways' in Haggai 1:5.

questions.question: According to Haggai 1:6, what is the result of the people's labor?
options: They sow much but bring in little
questions.correctAnswer: They sow much but bring in little
questions.explanation: The people sow much and bring in little; they eat but have not enough, as described in Haggai 1:6.

questions.question: What does the LORD say He will do if the people build the house?
options: Take pleasure in it and be glorified
Send them enemies to test them
questions.correctAnswer: Take pleasure in it and be glorified
questions.explanation: The LORD promises to take pleasure in the house and be glorified if they build it, as in Haggai 1:8.

questions.question: What reason does the LORD give for their lack of harvest and prosperity?
options: Because the LORD'S house is waste and they run every man to his own house
Because of the enemies surrounding them
questions.correctAnswer: Because the LORD'S house is waste and they run every man to his own house
questions.explanation: The LORD explains in Haggai 1:9 that their lack is because His house is waste and they are focused on their own houses.

questions.question: What has the LORD withheld from the people because of their actions?
options: Dew from heaven and fruit from the earth
questions.correctAnswer: Dew from heaven and fruit from the earth
questions.explanation: Haggai 1:10 states that heaven is stayed from dew and earth from her fruit due to their neglect.

questions.question: True or False: The drought mentioned in Haggai 1:11 affects only the crops.
questions.explanation: The drought affects the land, mountains, corn, new wine, oil, ground produce, men, cattle, and all labor as per Haggai 1:11.

questions.question: True or False: Zerubbabel and Joshua obeyed the voice of the LORD and the words of Haggai the prophet.
questions.explanation: Haggai 1:12 confirms they obeyed the voice of the LORD and the words of Haggai.

questions.question: True or False: Haggai told the people that the LORD was not with them.
questions.explanation: Haggai declared, 'I am with you, saith the LORD' in Haggai 1:13.

questions.question: True or False: The LORD stirred up the spirit of Zerubbabel, Joshua, and all the remnant of the people to work on the house of the LORD.
questions.explanation: According to Haggai 1:14, the LORD stirred up their spirits to work on the house of the LORD.

questions.question: In Haggai 1, which event happened first?
options: The LORD calling for a drought
The people building the house of the LORD
The word of the LORD coming to Zerubbabel and Joshua
The LORD stirring up the spirit of the people
questions.correctAnswer: The word of the LORD coming to Zerubbabel and Joshua
questions.explanation: The first event recorded is the word of the LORD coming to Zerubbabel and Joshua as stated in Haggai 1:1.

medium.title: Haggai Chapter 1 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from Haggai Chapter 1 to real-life situations.

questions.question: According to Haggai 1:6, what is the result of the people's labor?
options: They sow much but bring in little
They earn wages and save them
They are fully satisfied with food and drink
questions.correctAnswer: They sow much but bring in little
questions.explanation: Haggai 1:6 explains that the people have sown much but bring in little; they eat but are not satisfied, drink but are not filled, and wages are like putting money into a bag with holes.

questions.question: What command does the LORD give through Haggai in Haggai 1:8?
options: Go up to the mountain, bring wood, and build the house of the LORD
Stop working and wait for the right time
questions.correctAnswer: Go up to the mountain, bring wood, and build the house of the LORD
questions.explanation: Haggai 1:8 commands the people to bring wood from the mountain and build the house of the LORD, promising that God will take pleasure in it and be glorified.

questions.question: How does Haggai 1:7 relate to Haggai 1:6?
options: It repeats the same message in different words
It instructs the people to consider their ways because of the results described in verse 6
It shifts the topic to another issue
questions.correctAnswer: It instructs the people to consider their ways because of the results described in verse 6
questions.explanation: Haggai 1:7 follows verse 6 by urging the people to consider their ways, reflecting on why their labor yields little despite much effort.

questions.question: Why does the LORD say the people's efforts come to little in Haggai 1:9?
options: Because of the waste of the LORD's house and their focus on their own homes
Because they do not pray enough
questions.correctAnswer: Because of the waste of the LORD's house and their focus on their own homes
questions.explanation: Haggai 1:9 states that the people's efforts come to little because the LORD's house lies waste and they each run to their own house, neglecting the temple.

questions.question: What natural consequences does the LORD describe in Haggai 1:10 because of the people's neglect?
options: The heaven is stayed from dew and the earth from fruit
questions.correctAnswer: The heaven is stayed from dew and the earth from fruit
questions.explanation: Haggai 1:10 explains that because of their neglect, the heavens withhold dew and the earth fails to produce fruit, indicating divine displeasure.

questions.question: Based on Haggai 1:11, what has the LORD called upon the land and its produce?
options: A drought affecting all labor and produce
A time of peace and prosperity
questions.correctAnswer: A drought affecting all labor and produce
questions.explanation: Haggai 1:11 states that the LORD called for a drought upon the land, mountains, crops, new wine, oil, and all the labor of the hands, showing the severity of judgment.

questions.question: What does Haggai 1:12 indicate about the response of Zerubbabel, Joshua, and the remnant of the people?
options: They obeyed the voice of the LORD and feared before Him
questions.correctAnswer: They obeyed the voice of the LORD and feared before Him
questions.explanation: Haggai 1:12 describes that Zerubbabel, Joshua, and the remnant obeyed God's word delivered by Haggai and feared the LORD.

questions.question: According to Haggai 1:13, what assurance does the LORD give the people through His messenger?
options: You must build on your own strength
questions.explanation: Haggai 1:13 records the LORD's message through Haggai telling the people, "I am with you," to encourage them in their work.

questions.question: What does Haggai 1:14 say about the spirit of Zerubbabel, Joshua, and the people after the LORD's message?
options: Their spirit was discouraged and weak
The LORD stirred up their spirit to work on the house of the LORD
questions.correctAnswer: The LORD stirred up their spirit to work on the house of the LORD
questions.explanation: Haggai 1:14 explains that the LORD stirred up the spirit of Zerubbabel, Joshua, and the remnant to come and work on the temple.

questions.question: True or False: Haggai 1:6 illustrates that the people's clothing was warm and sufficient.
questions.explanation: Haggai 1:6 states that although they clothe themselves, there is none warm, indicating insufficiency in their clothing.

questions.question: True or False: According to Haggai 1:10, the withholding of dew and fruitfulness is a consequence of the people's neglect of God's house.
questions.explanation: Haggai 1:10 links the withholding of dew and fruitfulness directly to the people's neglect of the LORD's house, showing a cause-effect relationship.

questions.question: What does Haggai 1:7 promise if the people consider their ways in response to their current condition described in verse 6?
options: They will continue to suffer loss
They will find favor with the LORD and be restored
They must abandon the building project
questions.correctAnswer: They will find favor with the LORD and be restored
questions.explanation: While Haggai 1:7 itself commands consideration of ways, the surrounding verses (6-11) imply that turning to God's commands, including building His house, will bring restoration and blessing.

questions.question: How does the passage in Haggai 1:8-10 teach about the importance of prioritizing God's work over personal comfort?
options: It shows God rewards personal comfort first
It warns that neglecting God's house leads to loss and barrenness
It encourages focusing on personal houses only
It suggests delaying God's work is wise
questions.correctAnswer: It warns that neglecting God's house leads to loss and barrenness
questions.explanation: Haggai 1:8-10 contrasts the people's comfortable homes with the LORD's house lying waste, linking neglect to poor harvest and loss, teaching that God's work must be prioritized.

questions.question: In a scenario where a believer feels discouraged because their efforts seem fruitless, what biblical truth from Haggai 1:6-9 applies?
options: Their efforts are fruitless because God has abandoned them
Their lack of success may be due to neglecting God's priorities, such as rebuilding His house
They should give up and focus on personal comfort
Their labor will always be unsuccessful regardless
questions.correctAnswer: Their lack of success may be due to neglecting God's priorities, such as rebuilding His house
questions.explanation: Haggai 1:6-9 shows that despite much effort, their limited success is because God's house lies waste and they focus on their own homes, teaching the need to align with God's priorities.

questions.question: True or False: Haggai 1:11 shows that the LORD's judgment extended to both the land's produce and the people’s labor.
questions.explanation: Haggai 1:11 explicitly states the LORD called for a drought on the land, mountains, crops, new wine, oil, and all the labor of the hands, affecting both produce and people’s work.

hard.title: Haggai Chapter 1 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from Haggai Chapter 1.

questions.question: What specific calamity did the LORD call upon the land, mountains, corn, new wine, oil, ground, men, cattle, and labor according to Haggai 1?
questions.explanation: Haggai 1:11 explicitly states that the LORD called for a drought upon all these elements, showing divine judgment due to the people's neglect of His house.

questions.question: Who were the two leaders mentioned as obeying the LORD's voice and the words of Haggai the prophet?
questions.explanation: Haggai 1:12 identifies Zerubbabel the son of Shealtiel and Joshua the son of Josedech, the high priest, as the leaders who obeyed the LORD and Haggai's words.

questions.question: According to Haggai 1, what did Haggai say the LORD proclaimed to the people to encourage them?
questions.explanation: In Haggai 1:13, Haggai conveys the LORD's message of encouragement stating, 'I am with you,' strengthening the people's resolve to rebuild the temple.

questions.question: What action did the LORD stir up in Zerubbabel, Joshua, and the remnant of the people as recorded in Haggai 1?
options: To build their own houses first
To work in the house of the LORD
To offer sacrifices on the mountains
questions.correctAnswer: To work in the house of the LORD
questions.explanation: Haggai 1:14 says the LORD stirred up the spirit of Zerubbabel, Joshua, and the people so they came and did the work in the house of the LORD, showing divine empowerment for their task.

questions.question: On what day and month in the second year of Darius did the events of Haggai 1 conclude?
options: First day of the sixth month
Twenty-fourth day of the sixth month
Tenth day of the seventh month
First day of the first month
questions.correctAnswer: Twenty-fourth day of the sixth month
questions.explanation: The chapter closes with Haggai 1:15 stating the date as the twenty-fourth day of the sixth month in the second year of King Darius.

questions.question: What word in Haggai 1:5 and 1:7 is repeated to emphasize the need for self-examination?
questions.explanation: The word 'Consider' appears in Haggai 1:5 and 1:7 as a literary device of repetition urging the people to reflect on their ways.

questions.question: What does the Hebrew word for 'stirred up' in Haggai 1:14 (Hebrew: "ruach" meaning spirit or wind) imply about the nature of the LORD’s action on the leaders?
questions.explanation: The Hebrew word 'ruach' translated as 'spirit' here indicates God’s empowerment or inspiration of the leaders, stirring them to act, consistent with the meaning in Haggai 1:14.

questions.question: True or False: The drought mentioned in Haggai 1:11 affected both agricultural produce and living beings.
questions.explanation: Haggai 1:11 specifies that the drought affected corn, new wine, oil, ground produce, men, cattle, and all labor, showing a comprehensive impact.

questions.question: Which other Old Testament passage speaks of Zerubbabel as a signet ring, connecting to his role in Haggai 1?
questions.explanation: Zechariah 4:6-10 highlights Zerubbabel’s role as God’s chosen leader, symbolized as a signet ring, which complements his leadership in Haggai 1:12–14.

questions.question: What theme in Haggai 1 is echoed in Matthew 6:33 concerning priorities and seeking God's kingdom first?
questions.explanation: The theme in Haggai 1 of prioritizing the rebuilding of the LORD’s house before personal comfort aligns with Matthew 6:33’s teaching on seeking God's kingdom first.

questions.question: What literary device is present in Haggai 1:6 where the people sow much but bring in little, eat but have not enough, and earn wages to put into a bag with holes?
questions.explanation: Haggai 1:6 uses parallelism by repeating similar structures to emphasize the futility experienced by the people due to neglecting the LORD’s house.

questions.question: True or False: According to Haggai 1:9, the people's misfortune was because they focused on rebuilding the LORD’s house instead of their own houses.
questions.explanation: Haggai 1:9 states the opposite; misfortune came because the LORD’s house lay waste while each person ran to his own house, neglecting the temple.

questions.question: How does Haggai 1:10-11 describe the consequences of neglecting the LORD’s house in terms of nature?
options: Heaven stayed from dew and earth from fruit
questions.correctAnswer: Heaven stayed from dew and earth from fruit
questions.explanation: Haggai 1:10-11 explains that the heavens withheld dew and the earth produced no fruit as a direct consequence of neglecting God’s house.

questions.question: In the historical context of Haggai 1, under whose reign did these prophetic commands occur?
questions.explanation: Haggai 1:1 and 1:15 both specify the time as the second year of Darius the king, situating the prophecy historically in Persian rule.

questions.question: Which New Testament passage reflects the encouragement 'I am with you' found in Haggai 1:13?
questions.explanation: Matthew 28:20 contains Jesus’ promise 'I am with you always,' paralleling the LORD’s encouragement to Israel in Haggai 1:13.

theological.title: Haggai Chapter 1 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from Haggai Chapter 1 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: What does Haggai 1:2 reveal about the people's attitude towards rebuilding the LORD's house?
options: They believed it was time to build
They believed the time had not come
questions.correctAnswer: They believed the time had not come
questions.explanation: Haggai 1:2 states that the people said, 'The time is not come, the time that the LORD'S house should be built.' This indicates their belief that it was not the appropriate time for such a task.

questions.question: Which attribute of God is emphasized in Haggai 1:5 when He instructs the people to 'Consider your ways'?
questions.explanation: In Haggai 1:5, God calls the people to reflect on their actions, emphasizing His justice as He desires them to recognize their wrong priorities.

questions.question: What consequence does Haggai 1:10 mention as a result of the people's neglect of the LORD's house?
questions.explanation: Haggai 1:10 states, 'Therefore the heaven over you is stayed from dew, and the earth is stayed from her fruit,' indicating that neglecting God's house led to drought as a divine consequence.

questions.question: Haggai 1:11 describes a drought called by God. Which of the following does it NOT mention as affected?
questions.explanation: Haggai 1:11 lists corn, new wine, and cattle as affected by the drought, but it does not mention gold.

questions.question: What action does Haggai 1:8 command the people to take regarding the construction of the house?
questions.explanation: Haggai 1:8 instructs the people to 'Go up to the mountain, and bring wood, and build the house,' highlighting the need for their active participation in rebuilding.

questions.question: What does the phrase 'Consider your ways' in Haggai 1:7 imply about human responsibility?
options: God does not care about our choices
questions.explanation: The phrase 'Consider your ways' in Haggai 1:7 calls for self-examination, urging people to evaluate their priorities in light of their spiritual responsibilities.

questions.question: How does Haggai 1:12 demonstrate the response of Zerubbabel and Joshua to God's message?
options: They obeyed the voice of the LORD
questions.correctAnswer: They obeyed the voice of the LORD
questions.explanation: Haggai 1:12 shows that Zerubbabel, Joshua, and the remnant of the people 'obeyed the voice of the LORD their God,' indicating their positive response to God's command.

questions.question: What does the phrase 'I am with you' in Haggai 1:13 signify about God's relationship with His people?
questions.explanation: In Haggai 1:13, God's declaration 'I am with you' signifies His presence and assurance to the people as they undertake the task of rebuilding.

questions.question: Which theological theme is highlighted by the call to 'build the house' in Haggai 1:8?
questions.explanation: The call to 'build the house' in Haggai 1:8 emphasizes the theme of worship restoration, as the temple is central to Israel's worship practices.

questions.question: What does the instruction to 'bring wood' in Haggai 1:8 imply about the nature of the people's involvement?
options: It is solely a priestly duty
questions.explanation: The instruction to 'bring wood' in Haggai 1:8 indicates that rebuilding the house required communal participation, emphasizing collective responsibility.

questions.question: How does Haggai 1:9 reflect on the futility of the people's efforts?
options: They brought home little despite expecting much
questions.correctAnswer: They brought home little despite expecting much
questions.explanation: Haggai 1:9 states, 'Ye looked for much, and, lo, it came to little,' illustrating the futility of their efforts due to neglecting God's house.

questions.question: Sceptics claim that God does not intervene in worldly affairs. What does Haggai 1:11 teach about God's sovereignty over nature?
options: God calls for drought in response to sin
God only cares about spiritual matters
questions.correctAnswer: God calls for drought in response to sin
questions.explanation: Haggai 1:11 shows that God is actively involved in worldly affairs, as He calls for a drought in response to the people's neglect of His house, demonstrating His sovereignty.

questions.question: What does Haggai 1:14 reveal about the impact of God's message on the people's spirits?
questions.explanation: Haggai 1:14 indicates that the LORD stirred up the spirit of the people, leading them to work on the house of the LORD, reflecting a positive response to God's call.

questions.question: What combined teaching do Haggai 1:6 and 1:10 convey about the consequences of neglecting God's house?
options: Neglect leads to lack and hardship
We should not focus on material things
questions.correctAnswer: Neglect leads to lack and hardship
questions.explanation: Haggai 1:6 states that despite their efforts, the people brought in little, and 1:10 reveals that this is tied to God's withholding of dew and fruit, illustrating the consequences of neglecting God's house.

questions.question: What does Haggai 1:4 suggest about the disparity between the people's living conditions and the condition of the LORD's house?
options: God is pleased with their homes
They are living in luxury while God's house lies in ruins
They are equally invested in both
questions.correctAnswer: They are living in luxury while God's house lies in ruins
questions.explanation: Haggai 1:4 questions whether it is right for the people to dwell in cieled houses while the LORD's house lies waste, highlighting the disparity between their comfort and God's neglected house.
